description: MacroVoices #556 Luke Gromen: US Midterms & Beyond

turns.en: There's only one buyer, it's the Fed. Fed's gonna have to print money and buy treasuries and they will say, we're not monetizing the debt and we're not monetizing, then it'll all be bull crap.
turns.zh: 只有一个买家，那就是 Fed。Fed 将不得不印钞买国债，然后他们会说“我们不是在债务货币化，我们不是在货币化”，其实全都是一派胡言。

turns.en: That was Forrest for the Trees founder, Luke Grohman. I'm Eric Townsend and this is Macrovoices, the free weekly podcast targeting professional finance and sophisticated private investors.
turns.zh: 刚才那段话出自 Forrest for the Trees 创始人 Luke Gromen。我是 Eric Townsend，这里是 MacroVoices，一档面向专业金融人士和成熟个人投资者的免费周更播客。

turns.en: Episode 556 was produced on October 29th, 2026. Luke Grohman was ridiculed after his April 16th appearance on Macrovoices because many of our listeners thought his prediction that the Strait of Hormuz could remain closed as long as early July was outlandish.
turns.zh: 第 556 期节目制作于 2026 年 10 月 29 日。Luke Gromen 在 4 月 16 日做客 MacroVoices 之后遭到嘲笑，因为我们很多听众认为他预测霍尔木兹海峡（Strait of Hormuz）可能关闭到 7 月初，简直是天方夜谭。

turns.en: Now that the Strait has remained effectively closed for fully twice as long as Luke's outlandish prediction, we wanted to bring him back for an update.
turns.zh: 而现在，海峡实际关闭的时间已经是 Luke 那个“天方夜谭”预测的两倍有余，所以我们想请他回来做一次更新。

turns.en: And don't worry, we'll start with why the predictions that both Luke and I made for how bad the economic effects of that closure could be have so far yet to be realized.
turns.zh: 别担心，我们会先从这个问题谈起：为什么 Luke 和我当初对这场封锁会造成多严重经济影响的预测，到目前为止还没有兑现。

turns.en: And I'm Patrick Ceresna. Let's dive straight into this interview. Luke, it's great to get you back in the show. I want to cut to what I'm sure is already in everybody's mind, which is you were on this program on the 16th of April.
turns.zh: 我是 Patrick Ceresna。让我们直接进入今天的访谈。Luke，很高兴你能再次来到节目。我想先切入一个我确信所有人心里都在想的问题——你 4 月 16 号上过我们这档节目。

turns.en: Frankly, we got ridiculed when you said this situation in Iran could stretch out as long as the 4th of July. People thought it was crazy what is Luke Grohman smoking to think it could possibly go that long.
turns.zh: 坦白说，你说伊朗局势可能拖到 7 月 4 号的时候，我们被嘲笑了个遍。大家觉得这太疯了：Luke Gromen 到底是抽了什么，才会觉得事情能拖那么久。

turns.en: Well, now it's gone twice as long as that, but the predictions that both you and I made in terms of what the consequences would be for global financial markets and the global economy if the Strait of Hormuz stayed closed for even half as long as it's been closed, they really haven't materialized in the way that we feared.
turns.zh: 可现在，事情拖的时间已经是那个预测的两倍了。但你和我当时所做的预测——如果霍尔木兹海峡关闭的时间只有它实际关闭时长的一半，全球金融市场和全球经济会付出什么代价——那些后果并没有以我们担心的方式真正显现出来。

turns.en: So what's going on? Yeah, thanks for coming back on, Eric. Yeah, it is straight, it's still closed. It's Schrodinger's closure. So it's closed by both the Iranians and the Americans.
turns.zh: 那到底是怎么回事？——好的，谢谢你再请我来，Eric。是的，海峡确实还关着。这是一场薛定谔式的封锁（Schrödinger's closure）。所以按伊朗人的说法它是关着的，按美国人的说法它也是关着的。

turns.en: And depending on who you talk to, it is both closed and it is also fully open at the same time, according to President Trump. So what we got right was, yeah, the conflict is still going on.
turns.zh: 而且取决于你问的是谁，它既是关闭的，同时按 Trump 总统的说法又是完全开放的。所以我们说对的部分是：没错，冲突还在继续。

turns.en: There are still constrictions to supply to some degree. What we got wrong was how quickly it would take to ripple through. And then I think there's multiple reasons for that.
turns.zh: 供应在某种程度上仍然受到挤压。我们说错的部分，是它传导扩散的速度。我觉得背后有好几个原因。

turns.en: Number one, underestimated the degree to which China would constrain its demand and run down its SPR reserves initially. And that was a big part of it.
turns.zh: 第一，我们低估了中国压制自身需求、并在初期消耗自己 SPR（战略石油储备，Strategic Petroleum Reserve）库存的程度。这是很重要的一部分原因。

turns.en: And then the second part and also other Western SPRs, the United States in particular and others, right? So there's been a coordinated effort.
turns.zh: 第二部分，还有其他西方国家的 SPR，尤其是美国以及其他一些国家，对吧？所以这是一次协同行动。

turns.en: So that was more supply that came on and that mitigated things. And then I think the second thing as it relates to some of the food, et cetera stuff, it's kind of this, it's a slightly different version of the same thing that we're finding here, which is this is going to take a lot longer than expected, as we said initially.
turns.zh: 这就带来了更多供应，从而缓和了局面。然后我认为第二件事，跟粮食等等那块有关，其实和我们在这里发现的是同一个问题的略微不同的版本，也就是：这件事会拖得比我们最初说的要长得多。

turns.en: I think part of the food and fertilizer thing might be, and when I say might, I'm hearing that it's the case, at least in certain emerging markets, is fertilizers just too expensive to order, so they're just not going to order it.
turns.zh: 我觉得粮食和化肥这块的问题可能在于——我说“可能”，但我听到说至少在某些新兴市场确实如此——化肥实在太贵了，根本下不起单，所以他们干脆就不订了。

turns.en: And so paradoxically, the first stage of a real problem that will show up in food inflation around the world, it's not going to show up this year.
turns.zh: 所以自相矛盾的是，真正会体现为全球粮食通胀的第一阶段问题，今年并不会显现出来。

turns.en: It's going to show up in theory in lower yields next year if fertilizer isn't bought and applied and therefore yields are down. And so paradoxically, that might be some of what we're saying.
turns.zh: 理论上它会在明年体现为更低的产量——如果化肥没有被购买、没有被施用，那么单产就会下降。所以自相矛盾的是，这可能正是我们所说的那部分原因。

turns.en: It's not like we've lost 2 billion people. So in theory, they're still eating. So what a little bit that I've read on it is that on the margin, demand for fertilizers down because no one can afford it.
turns.zh: 这并不是说我们少了 20 亿人。所以理论上他们还在吃饭。我就这个话题读到的一点情况是：在边际上，化肥需求下降了，因为没人买得起。

turns.en: The marginal farmer around the world, particularly in lower income places, can't afford it. And so paradoxically, and something that's ultimately very, very bullish for prices, for crop prices, row crop prices, initially, it might actually be somewhat bearish.
turns.zh: 全球范围内的边际农民，尤其是在低收入地区，买不起化肥。所以自相矛盾的是，一件最终对作物价格、对大宗农作物价格极度看涨的事情，在初期反而可能有点利空。

turns.en: And that's been, I think, somewhat confusing to me. And maybe that's sort of first world privilege of like, hey, I know this is a problem, so I would stockpile, but that's as opposed to I just can't afford it, so I just don't buy it.
turns.zh: 这一点我觉得多少让我有点困惑。也许这算是一种第一世界的特权吧——“嘿，我知道这是个问题，所以我会囤货”，而不是“我就是买不起，所以我干脆不买”。

turns.en: The math doesn't make sense. I'm not going to plant whatever the case may be. But we'll see. Luke, what I just cannot get my head around is when this first began, as you said, really what happened was there were massive SPR releases coordinated around the world.
turns.zh: 账算不过来。我就不种了，诸如此类。但我们走着瞧。——Luke，我实在想不明白的是：这件事刚开始的时候，正如你所说，真正发生的是全球范围内协同的大规模 SPR 投放。

turns.en: All the experts that I'm seeing in the oil market are saying, yeah, you know what? We've used up most of the available supply buffers. We've done all of those big releases.
turns.zh: 我在石油市场看到的所有专家都在说：是啊，你知道吗？我们已经把大部分可用的供应缓冲都用掉了，那些大规模投放我们都做完了。

turns.en: Now we're getting to the point where we don't really have a lot of strategic reserves left. Now China still has plenty. They have been reducing their imports.
turns.zh: 现在我们正走到这样一个节点：我们其实已经没有多少战略储备剩下了。当然中国还有很多，他们一直在减少进口。

turns.en: That's, as you said, contributed tremendously. But the thing is, we're still seeing refineries, particularly Russian refineries being struck by Ukraine, but also in Saudi Arabia and in Iran.
turns.zh: 正如你所说，这贡献了非常大的缓冲。但问题是，我们仍然看到炼油厂——尤其是俄罗斯的炼油厂——被乌克兰打击，沙特和伊朗境内也有。

turns.en: If we take refineries out and we reduce the global capacity for refining products, refineries take 10 years to build. So yes, we're having a crack spread blowout, I suppose, but it doesn't seem to me that the news is really picking up on the fact that the damage we're doing to refining capacity could be permanent, not permanent, but persistent for many years after the war finally ends.
turns.zh: 如果我们把炼油厂打掉，削减了全球的成品油炼化能力，那么炼油厂是要 10 年才能建起来的。所以没错，我们算是看到裂解价差（crack spread）暴涨了，但在我看来，新闻并没有真正抓住这一点：我们对炼化产能造成的损害可能不是永久性的，但在战争最终结束之后的很多年里都会持续存在。

turns.en: Would you agree with that? And why isn't the market freaking out more than it is? It's a great question. It's one of these things that as a tourist, I don't fully understand, right?
turns.zh: 你同意这个判断吗？为什么市场没有比现在更恐慌？——这是个好问题。这属于那种作为一个“游客”（tourist）我并不能完全理解的事情，对吧？

turns.en: Because in one hand, my president's telling me that the straight is nearly up and running. Okay, so there's more oil supply globally. Okay. And SPRs are being run down, as you know, to around the world.
turns.zh: 因为一方面，我们总统告诉我海峡差不多已经恢复通航了。好，那么全球石油供应就更多了。好。而且你也知道，全世界的 SPR 都在被消耗。

turns.en: Okay, there's more supply. And the damage to refineries that you just listed off around the world would suggest that there's less demand for oil from those refineries, which in theory, when you sort of add that up, that's a lot of incremental crude.
turns.zh: 好，供应更多了。而你刚才列举的全球各地炼油厂受损，则意味着这些炼油厂对原油的需求减少了。理论上把这些加总起来，那就是大量的增量原油。

turns.en: Now versus, say, six months ago. Four months ago. And yet the price of crude is where it is higher, much higher than six months ago, and certainly eight months ago.
turns.zh: 现在跟六个月前比、跟四个月前比。可是原油价格却还在现在这个位置——比六个月前高，而且肯定比八个月前高得多。

turns.en: And, you know, you are seeing signs of strain. Obviously, you know, diesel prices in certain parts of the world are approaching $200 a barrel.
turns.zh: 而且你确实能看到紧张的迹象。显然，世界上某些地区的柴油价格正在逼近每桶 200 美元。

turns.en: So you are getting some of those numbers that some of the sort of, you know, quote unquote, doomers thought we'd get to. But I don't fully understand, you know, is China taking it all down?
turns.zh: 所以你确实在看到一些数字，一些所谓“末日论者”（doomers）以为我们会达到的数字。但我并不完全理解，你知道，是不是中国把这一切都吃下去了？

turns.en: And that's the missing point. And we've certainly seen data suggesting that China has increased its purchases in recent months off the lows and continues to increase them.
turns.zh: 这就是缺失的那一环。我们确实看到数据显示，中国最近几个月的采购量已经从低点回升，并且在继续增加。

turns.en: And so, you know, that is a fact pattern that would, in theory, square the circle of SPR's rundown refineries not buying as much, because a number of them are offline.
turns.zh: 所以这是一个理论上能够把这一圈说法自洽起来的事实链条：SPR 在被消耗、炼油厂因为不少停工而少买原油、

turns.en: Strait of Hormuz is seeing very good volumes and there's no problems there. Is China just buying it all? I don't know if that's something that makes sense, but I just don't know because like you, I'm a little bit scratch in my head based, again, as a tourist just watching sort of general flows of directions, it doesn't quite make sense to me, given the narratives that I'm being told as an American.
turns.zh: 霍尔木兹海峡的通行量却非常好、那边没有任何问题。是不是中国把这一切都买走了？我不知道这个说法是否讲得通，但我就是不知道——因为我和你一样，我也有点摸不着头脑。同样作为一个只是大致观察流向和方向的“游客”，这跟我作为一个美国人被灌输的那些叙事对不上。

turns.en: We recorded this interview on Tuesday afternoon, October 27th, so two days before our listeners will hear it, and exactly one week before the US presidential election.
turns.zh: 我们这次访谈是在 10 月 27 日周二下午录制的，也就是比听众听到它早两天，距离美国总统选举正好一周。

turns.en: So it seems like if I'm reading the tea leaves correctly, the escalation or re-escalation by the United States, if that's what is to happen, is probably been put off until after the election.
turns.zh: 所以看起来——如果我没看错这些蛛丝马迹的话——美国的升级或者再度升级，如果真会发生，大概已经被推迟到选举之后了。

turns.en: Is that your read and what do you expect both between now and the election and also after the election in terms of this conflict? Yeah, my view on the conflict has been pretty consistent the whole time, which is that Iran has more leverage than the Western narrative suggests because Iran doesn't have to beat the US, it just has to beat the bond market.
turns.zh: 这是你的判断吗？从现在到选举之间、以及选举之后，你对这场冲突有什么预期？——是的，我对这场冲突的看法一直相当一致：伊朗拥有的筹码比西方叙事所暗示的要多，因为伊朗不需要打败美国，它只需要打败债券市场。

turns.en: And when I said that on February 27th, same thing, people laughed at me, 10-year yield was at 3.94%. A couple of weeks ago when we hit 5.3% on the 10-year, nobody was laughing anymore.
turns.zh: 我在 2 月 27 号说这句话的时候，同样被人嘲笑，当时 10 年期收益率是 3.94%。几周前 10 年期涨到 5.3% 的时候，就没人笑了。

turns.en: And we've gotten a bit of a respite there, but I still think there is a level of hubris or non-understanding of what the Iranians need to do and are doing and will likely continue to do, which is the Iranians understand the production rate, the resupply rate of US air defense missiles.
turns.zh: 之后我们稍微喘了口气，但我仍然认为，对于伊朗人需要做什么、正在做什么、并且很可能继续做什么，美方存在一种自大或者说是不理解。伊朗人清楚美国防空导弹的生产速率和补库速率。

turns.en: And they understand that resupplying those air defense missiles can be done at, say, I don't know what the right number is, let's just pick a number for easy math to make an example.
turns.zh: 他们也明白，补充这些防空导弹的速度，比如说——我不知道确切数字是多少，我们随便挑一个数好算账、举个例子。

turns.en: They can replenish 100 missiles a month. So let's say we can make 100 air defense missiles a month. Assuming the Chinese keep sending us rare earths at the same pace they have been at times in the past, that's not necessarily true, but let's just set that aside for now.
turns.zh: 他们每月能补充 100 枚导弹。那就假设我们每月能生产 100 枚防空导弹。前提是中国人继续以他们过去某些时候的节奏向我们供应稀土——这一点未必成立，但我们先把它放一边。

turns.en: US can replenish 100 missiles a month in our fictitious example here. The Iranians understand that and they understand that all they need to do is keep lobbing drones and missiles at us in a manner that forces us to use 150 to 200 to 300 air defense missiles per month.
turns.zh: 在我们这个虚构的例子里，美国每月能补充 100 枚导弹。伊朗人明白这一点，他们也明白自己需要做的，就是持续向我们投射无人机和导弹，逼我们每月用掉 150 枚、200 枚、300 枚防空导弹。

turns.en: And they understand that at that point, it's just not that complex a line theory calculation. The Americans burn 200 to 300 missiles a month.
turns.zh: 他们明白，到了那个时候，这在理论上就不是一个多复杂的计算：美国人每月消耗 200 到 300 枚导弹。

turns.en: The Americans can only replace 100 missiles a month. The Americans are going to run out of air defense missiles on ex-date and when they do, then we can hit them with impunity.
turns.zh: 美国人每月只能补充 100 枚。美国人的防空导弹会在某个确定的日期耗尽，而一旦耗尽，我们就可以肆无忌惮地打击他们。

turns.en: They will pull resources from other strategic regions which will make them look weak and sooner or later, they will have to fold before us. That's been the calculus the whole time.
turns.zh: 他们会从其他战略区域抽调资源，那会让他们显得很虚弱，迟早他们必须在我们面前让步。这从一开始就是他们的算计。

turns.en: And this is understood in the US complex, the US defense and intelligence complex. Whether the Trump administration wants to continue pretending it isn't true or not, I think is the $64,000 question.
turns.zh: 而且这一点在美国的国防与情报体系内部是被理解的。至于 Trump 政府是否愿意继续假装它不是真的，我认为这就是那个 6.4 万美元的大问题（the $64,000 question）。

turns.en: And we've seen in the last couple of weeks slash months, more things that I was getting laughed at six months ago around, I was hearing that US military bases were taking very serious damage, that we were unable to provide air defense for them.
turns.zh: 而在过去几周／几个月里，我们已经看到更多我在六个月前说了会被嘲笑的事情。我当时听说美军基地正在遭受非常严重的损失，我们无法为它们提供防空保护。

turns.en: And people are like, oh, you're crazy. And that has come out as the case. And here too, the Iranians understand the Americans are not going to station troops in the Middle East at a base for which they cannot provide air defense.
turns.zh: 大家当时的反应是：哦，你疯了。而这已经被证实确有其事。这里同样，伊朗人明白，美国人不会把部队驻扎在中东那些他们无法提供防空保护的基地里。

turns.en: And the Americans cannot invade. There's all these talks of let's put boots on the ground. America has not fought a war without air superiority, air dominance in 80 years.
turns.zh: 而且美国人无法入侵。到处都在谈论“让我们派地面部队上去”。美国已经 80 年没有在没有空中优势、没有制空权的情况下打过仗了。

turns.en: Americans don't know what that is. I mean, there's protocols for it, but they're messy. They're very messy, right? You don't just get to like do what we did in 91, where you assemble a couple hundred thousand troops in the desert in tents and like nothing happens.
turns.zh: 美国人不知道那是什么滋味。我是说，确实有相应的预案，但那些预案很混乱，非常混乱，对吧？你不可能像我们 1991 年那样，在沙漠里搭起帐篷集结几十万人，然后什么事都不会发生。

turns.en: That's not how that works. It looks more like, hey, here come the boats in the beginning of saving private Ryan, except with missiles and drones that you can't provide enough air defense for.
turns.zh: 事情不是那样运作的。它看起来更像是《拯救大兵瑞恩》（Saving Private Ryan）开头那些冲上岸的船，只不过换成的是导弹和无人机，而你无法提供足够的防空来应对。

turns.en: So like I give all of this sort of background context rant. Again, I'm sure I'm screwing a few things up. This is how it's been explained to me in again, very directional flow terms.
turns.zh: 所以我讲了这么一大段背景性的吐槽。再说一遍，我肯定有些地方说得不对。这就是别人向我解释的方式，同样只是非常粗略的方向性流向。

turns.en: But the point here is that if I'm the Iranians, why stop? Why would I stop this? Especially I'm getting resupplied by the Russians and or the Chinese, which is, if you're the Russians and the Chinese, especially the Russians, the Russians have been being shot at by the Americans via the Ukrainians.
turns.zh: 但这里的要点是：如果我是伊朗人，为什么要停？我为什么要停下来？尤其是当我还在从俄罗斯人和／或中国人那里获得补给的时候。如果你是俄罗斯人和中国人——尤其是俄罗斯人——俄罗斯人一直在被美国人通过乌克兰人射击。

turns.en: I mean, let's be clear. We've been putting in the targeting and the reconnaissance data in for the Ukrainians. We do everything for them except hit the fire button with missiles launching at Russian soil.
turns.zh: 我是说，讲清楚一点：目标数据和侦察数据都是我们在为乌克兰人提供。除了最后按下发射导弹打击俄罗斯本土的那个按钮，其他所有事情都是我们替他们做的。

turns.en: And so if you're the Russians all day long, you're like, oh, great. We'll keep supplying you Iran. You just keep doing this. We'll keep helping you with satellite targeting around.
turns.zh: 所以如果你是俄罗斯人，你整天都在想：哦，太好了。我们会继续给伊朗供货，你就继续这么干。我们会继续帮你做卫星定位之类的事情。

turns.en: Just keep doing this. Because the open secret at that level is they know the Americans can't replenish missiles beyond whatever that rate is, was 100 missiles a month, 120.
turns.zh: 你就继续这么干。因为在那个层面，公开的秘密是：他们知道美国人无法以超过某个速率补充导弹——不管那个速率是每月 100 枚还是 120 枚。

turns.en: And that number's going up slowly, but it's not going up nearly fast enough. And again, it really can't go up faster than the Iranians can force us to use what we already have.
turns.zh: 而且这个数字在缓慢上升，但远远跟不上。同样，它的提升速度真的不可能快过伊朗人逼迫我们消耗现有库存的速度。

turns.en: And so when you say, what do I think is going to happen? I think it's going to continue dragging on because I think the Iranians are happy to have it drag on.
turns.zh: 所以当你问我觉得会发生什么？我觉得它会继续拖下去，因为我认为伊朗人乐于让它拖下去。

turns.en: I think the Russians are happy to have it drag on. I think the Chinese are happy to have it drag on. I don't think the Israelis mind it because we shoulder the burden for them.
turns.zh: 我认为俄罗斯人乐于让它拖下去。我认为中国人乐于让它拖下去。我不认为以色列人介意，因为是我们在替他们扛这个负担。

turns.en: And then instead of those missiles will just be coming down on them. And in the meantime, it makes the administration more and more and more unpopular.
turns.zh: 否则那些导弹就会直接落在他们头上。而与此同时，这会让这届政府越来越、越来越不得人心。

turns.en: And it may be a key reason why if he loses next week, it's going to be a key reason why he loses. Luke, the other thing that our listeners will have learned that we don't know yet is the outcome of tomorrow's FOMC meeting.
turns.zh: 而且这可能是一个关键原因：如果他下周输了，这就会是他输掉的关键原因之一。——Luke，另一件我们的听众听到这期节目时还不知道结果的事情，是明天 FOMC 会议的结果。

turns.en: What's your outlook? And what do you think about this backup in rates? You mentioned the 10-year earlier. Let's go a little deeper on that. Where do you think we're headed?
turns.zh: 你的展望是什么？你怎么看这轮利率上行？你刚才提到了 10 年期。我们在这上面再深入一点。你觉得我们会走向哪里？

turns.en: Yeah, the backup on the 10-year yield to me was really interesting and potentially notable from last week. So I guess I'll answer the Fed question first.
turns.zh: 是的，上周 10 年期收益率的这轮上行，在我看来非常有趣，也可能很值得注意。所以我先回答 Fed 的问题。

turns.en: I don't have a strong feeling. I think he's either going to hold tighter or he's going to raise rates to 25 basis points. I don't know that it matters a whole lot right now.
turns.zh: 我没有很强的判断。我觉得他要么按兵不动、维持更紧，要么加息 25 个基点（bps）。我不认为这在当下有多大关系。

turns.en: I think raising rates all else equal is the wrong thing. But I think this backup in rates last week, the 10-year fell as much as 20 basis points intraday, which is I mean, I've been in investment research for 31 years.
turns.zh: 我认为在其他条件相同的情况下，加息是错误的事情。但我觉得上周这轮利率上行——10 年期盘中一度下跌了多达 20 个基点——我是说，我做投资研究已经 31 年了。

turns.en: I could probably count on one hand the number of days that the 10-year treasury yield fell 20 basis points and I guess it's 9-11, Lehman, the handful of sort of catastrophes that have happened, COVID in my career.
turns.zh: 10 年期国债收益率单日下跌 20 个基点的日子，我大概一只手就数得过来，我想也就是 9·11、Lehman、以及我职业生涯中发生过的那几场灾难，还有 COVID。

turns.en: And so on some random Thursday and furthermore, it was a real disconnection from the existing market regime. And what I mean by that is I got down to my screens on Thursday morning and I sort of run through a list of prices just to check in on them and just see, gives me an idea of sort of what's happening, right?
turns.zh: 所以在某个平平无奇的周四出现这种走势，而且它还与当时既有的市场机制完全脱节。我这么说的意思是：周四早上我坐到屏幕前，我大致会过一遍一串价格，只是查看一下，让我对正在发生什么有个概念，对吧？

turns.en: So now, click up gold. OK, gold is down 50 bucks. OK, well, all right, if gold's down 50 bucks, then that means oil's up big. Call up oil, oil's up 3%.
turns.zh: 所以我先点开黄金。好，黄金跌了 50 美元。好，那么行，如果黄金跌了 50 美元，那就意味着原油大涨。点开原油，原油涨了 3%。

turns.en: OK, that makes sense. OK, well, if gold's down big and oil's up big, that means Bitcoin, which is sort of a Texas, yes, or Texas hedge read on liquidity, what's happening, I bet your Bitcoin's down big.
turns.zh: 好，这说得通。好，那么如果黄金大跌、原油大涨，那就意味着 Bitcoin——它某种程度上是对流动性状况的一个“德州对冲”（Texas hedge）式读数——我打赌 Bitcoin 大跌。

turns.en: Sure enough, Bitcoin on Thursday last week, down 3% or something, 4%. OK, that all makes sense. Well, if those three things nailed that, I said, OK, so dollar's probably up DXY.
turns.zh: 果然，上周四 Bitcoin 跌了 3% 左右，或者 4%。好，这一切都说得通。那么如果这三样都对上了，我说，好，那美元大概涨了，看 DXY（美元指数）。

turns.en: And it was like, oh, it's up a little, but it's not up a ton. But OK, but it's up. And suddenly, finally, all of that means that the 10-year treasury yield should be up big today.
turns.zh: 结果是：哦，涨了一点，但没有涨很多。但好，它确实涨了。然后突然之间，所有这些都意味着今天 10 年期国债收益率应该大涨。

turns.en: And I call it the 10-year treasury yield, I'm just like, ooh, it's down big. That's different. That doesn't make sense. That's why. And is this a one-off, or is this some sort of recognition around whether it's France, whether it's Middle East, whether it's Iran, or whether it's a recognition that the Trump administration is going to lose, and they're going to do something that ensures that markets really sell off as a result?
turns.zh: 我点开 10 年期国债收益率，然后我就：哦，它大跌。这不一样。这说不通。这就是原因。那么这是一次性的，还是某种认知转变？不管是因为法国、因为中东、因为伊朗，还是因为市场认识到 Trump 政府将会输掉选举，而他们将会做某件确保市场因此真正大跌的事情？

turns.en: Because, I mean, what Trump has said, I think six or seven different times in the last month that if the Democrats win, we will get a 1929-style depression.
turns.zh: 因为我是说，Trump 在过去一个月里我想已经说了六七次：如果民主党赢了，我们将会迎来一场 1929 年式的大萧条。

turns.en: Besant has warned slash threatened that if the Democrats win, he will be forced to do his planned fiscal consolidation in the span of two months from November 4th through January 3rd, 2027.
turns.zh: Bessent 也警告过／威胁过：如果民主党赢了，他将被迫在 11 月 4 日到 2027 年 1 月 3 日这两个月的时间内完成他计划中的财政紧缩。

turns.en: He's going to have to do all of his fiscal cutting, which fits both gentlemen's personalities perfectly, which is right, which is, if I can't win at monopoly, I'm going to just dump over the board.
turns.zh: 他将不得不做所有的财政削减。而这完全符合这两位先生的个性，也就是——没错——如果我玩《大富翁》（Monopoly）赢不了，我就直接把棋盘掀了。

turns.en: And that's what that would look like for markets. And if their internal polling was saying, hey, you're going to lose at least the House on next Tuesday, look, we know from oil markets that somebody, I won't say they, because I don't know that for a fact.
turns.zh: 对市场来说就会是那个样子。而如果他们的内部民调显示：嘿，下周二你至少会输掉众议院。听着，我们从石油市场上知道，有人——我不会说是“他们”，因为我并没有事实依据。

turns.en: It's very strong suspicions. But I don't know it for a fact, but somebody was giving somebody else very big heads up before Trump would tweet something as it related to the war in oil markets.
turns.zh: 这是非常强烈的怀疑，但我没有事实依据——不过在 Trump 就战争与石油市场发推之前，有人在给另外一些人提供非常大的提前消息。

turns.en: And then we also know from two weeks ago, when the CFTC went to investigate, who that was, they were told to stand down by the Trump administration.
turns.zh: 而且我们还从两周前知道，当 CFTC 去调查那是谁干的时候，他们被 Trump 政府叫停了。

turns.en: That investigation. Is it possible that part of what we saw last week in the tenure breaking the correlation or anything else and falling in a way that has literally only has happened in 30 years on catastrophic days, was that somebody in markets getting a heads up from the administration that, hey, we're going to lose.
turns.zh: 那项调查。有没有可能，上周我们看到的一部分情况——10 年期打破相关性、以一种 30 年来只在灾难性日子才出现过的方式下跌——是因为市场上有人从政府那里得到了提前消息：嘿，我们要输了。

turns.en: And when we lose, we're going to dump the board over, which is to say, we are going to try to implement fiscal consolidation in two months. And when that happens, stocks are going to tank, commodities are going to tank, and you're going to want to own bonds.
turns.zh: 而当我们输的时候，我们要把棋盘掀了。也就是说，我们要在两个月内推行财政紧缩。而一旦那样，股票会暴跌，大宗商品会暴跌，你会想要持有债券。

turns.en: That strikes me as very possible, given what Trump and Besant have been warning. Besant more eloquently than Trump, but they're basically saying the same thing.
turns.zh: 考虑到 Trump 和 Bessent 一直在警告的内容，我觉得这非常有可能。Bessent 说得比 Trump 更有水准，但他们基本上在说同一件事。

turns.en: So that to me was super interesting. And I don't know quite what to make of it. You know, since then, 10 years basically hasn't moved. It's basically been pinned at 499 since Thursday.
turns.zh: 所以那在我看来超级有意思。我也不太知道该怎么解读。你知道，从那以后 10 年期基本没动过，自周四以来基本被钉在 4.99% 上。

turns.en: Now this is Tuesday, right? So we're talking about a grand total of three trading days. So I don't want to play too much a five minute macro, but that Thursday move in 10 year yields to me was very noteworthy, peculiar, didn't fit.
turns.zh: 现在是周二，对吧？所以我们总共只讲了三个交易日。所以我不想搞太多“五分钟宏观”（five minute macro），但周四 10 年期收益率的那个走势在我看来非常值得注意、非常反常、对不上。

turns.en: And those are the types of things that really get my spidey sense up. Luke, let's turn to the equity market, which has been rallying really pretty briskly since the beginning of April, but we just broke a ascending wedge pattern to the downside.
turns.zh: 而这类事情正是真正让我“蜘蛛感应”（spidey sense）竖起来的东西。——Luke，我们转向股票市场。它自 4 月初以来一直涨得相当迅猛，但我们刚刚向下突破了一个上升楔形（ascending wedge）形态。

turns.en: We had a fair bit of turbulence in the last few weeks. And you know, I'm looking at this, I'm saying, okay, markets hate uncertainty, and we're headed in just next week to the midterm elections, as you just described.
turns.zh: 过去几周我们经历了相当大的动荡。你知道，我看着这个走势，心里想：好吧，市场讨厌不确定性，而下周我们就要进入中期选举了，正如你刚才描述的那样。

turns.en: Is that what this is about? Or is this AI credit bubble and AI capex boom actually at risk of a bust, which everybody's been worried about for months and months and months, is that finally coming to a head?
turns.zh: 这就是原因吗？还是说这个 AI 信贷泡沫和 AI 资本开支繁荣，其实真的面临破裂风险——这是大家几个月来一直担心的事情——是不是终于要到临界点了？

turns.en: I can't tell which it is. What are your thoughts? Yeah, I can't either. I think there's probably elements of both. And it's weird because in theory, based on what the Washington hands that I've read, because it's not my Ballywick, based on people whose Ballywick it is, they've said that if you get some sort of big blue win, it's actually really good for liquidity because nothing will get done and everything,
turns.zh: 我分辨不出是哪一个。你怎么看？——是的，我也分辨不出。我觉得两者可能都有成分。而且很奇怪，因为理论上，根据我读到的那些华盛顿圈内人的说法——那不是我的专业领域，而是那些以此为专业的人——他们说，如果出现某种“大蓝色胜利”（big blue win），那其实对流动性非常好，因为什么都不会通过，一切都会变成——

turns.en: it'll be a horse trading of you spend your money the way you want and you give me to spend money who I want and nothing gets cut. And that in theory would be good for bad for the dollar, good for gold, good for stocks.
turns.zh: ——一场讨价还价的交易：你按你想的方式花你的钱，你给我按我想的方式花钱，最后什么都不会被削减。理论上那会是好事：利空美元、利好黄金、利好股票。

turns.en: But if there's uncertainty around the election or if Trump contests the election, as I've seen serious people talking about in certain areas and it drags out, that wouldn't be good for risk.
turns.zh: 但如果选举结果存在不确定性，或者如果 Trump 对选举结果提出异议——我看到一些严肃的人在特定领域讨论这种可能——并且拖下去，那对风险资产就不会是好事。

turns.en: I wouldn't think so. I think that uncertainty point around the election, I think that's very well taken. And then I do think the credit side of what we're seeing on AI, and then the secondary credit side, which I think is still very early days, right?
turns.zh: 我可不敢那么说。我觉得你关于选举不确定性的那个观点非常到位。然后我确实认为，我们在 AI 上看到的信贷层面问题，以及那个我认为是二阶导数的信贷层面问题——我觉得还处在非常早期的阶段，对吧？

turns.en: We're seeing tons of discussion around, hey, what are Oracle credit default swaps doing? What are other hyperscalar credit default swaps doing?
turns.zh: 我们看到大量讨论围绕：嘿，Oracle 的信用违约互换（credit default swaps，CDS）在什么价位？其他超大规模云服务商（hyperscaler）的 CDS 在什么价位？

turns.en: And where is this deal priced? And some of the circular financing concerns and all those things. And I get those things. And there's a second derivative credit concern that I'm still seeing basically nobody talked about.
turns.zh: 这笔交易定价在哪里？以及一些循环融资（circular financing）的担忧等等。这些我都理解。而还有第二层导数的信贷担忧，我发现基本上没有人在谈论。

turns.en: I've posted on X a couple of times about it. I've been writing about it for clients for several months now. But it is the dynamic that there is $19 trillion in consumer debt outstanding.
turns.zh: 我在 X 上发过几次，我也已经为客户写了好几个月了。但就是这个动态：目前有 19 万亿美元的未偿消费债务。

turns.en: Mortgages, credit cards, auto loans primarily. And that means, so it will 5% of that number is call it a trillion dollars for easy math. So if you assume that AI is going to really displace a lot of white collar jobs, and I think there's been a pretty robust debate around that.
turns.zh: 主要是房贷、信用卡、汽车贷款。这意味着——所以这个数字的 5%，为了方便计算就算作 1 万亿美元吧。所以如果你假设 AI 真的会取代大量白领岗位——我认为围绕这一点一直有一场相当激烈的辩论。

turns.en: I think it's foolish to think they won't, but there's been a robust debate about it. But I think in the last literally two weeks, the side saying that AI is going to create a lot of white collar job loss has started to strike some serious body blows to the side that everything is gonna be fine for white collar jobs.
turns.zh: 我认为觉得它们不会被取代是愚蠢的，但确实有一场激烈的辩论。不过我认为，就在最近这两周，主张 AI 将造成大量白领失业的那一方，已经开始对“白领岗位一切都会没事”的那一方打出几记沉重的重拳。

turns.en: You had Kroger, talk about laying off, I think 37% of their corporate workforce. Kroger's business model hasn't changed in a long time. They sell food, right?
turns.zh: 你有 Kroger 谈到要裁掉——我想是——他们公司总部员工的 37%。Kroger 的商业模式很久没有变过了。他们卖食品，对吧？

turns.en: So this is AI related. American Express last week came out and said we are firing 5% of workers because AI. Barclays came out last week, said we're firing 5% of workers because AI.
turns.zh: 所以这跟 AI 有关。American Express 上周出来说：我们要裁掉 5% 的员工，因为 AI。Barclays 上周出来说：我们要裁掉 5% 的员工，因为 AI。

turns.en: And then of course yesterday, Microsoft is buying out 27% of their workforce. Yikes. And the reason I bring up these numbers, and this is the credit side that people just, the second derivative credit side that no one is talking about.
turns.zh: 然后当然，昨天，Microsoft 正在买断其 27% 的员工。哎哟。我之所以提出这些数字，这就是那个信贷层面——那个没人谈论的二阶导数信贷层面。

turns.en: And I think they're not talking about it because there's nothing to say. There's nothing to say. Which is all of these people getting laid off, they're not gonna find another job.
turns.zh: 而且我认为他们之所以不谈论它，是因为没什么可说的。真的没什么可说的。那就是：所有这些被裁掉的人，他们不会再找到另一份工作。

turns.en: Not easily and probably not at the same wage because the AI is hitting everybody all at the same time in finance and tech in particular, but white collar more broadly.
turns.zh: 不会容易找到，而且大概不会以同样的工资找到，因为 AI 在同一时间打击所有人，尤其是金融和科技行业，但更广泛地说是所有白领。

turns.en: And if you just kind of play that out over several quarters, that $19 trillion in consumer loans, let's pretend 5% of those default as a result of AI.
turns.zh: 而如果你把这个推演几个季度，那 19 万亿美元的消费贷款，我们就假设其中 5% 因为 AI 而违约。

turns.en: Just sometime in the next two years, three years. 5%, that's roughly a trillion dollars. So by way of comparison, the entire equity capital base of the United States banking system, according to the Fed is $2.6 trillion.
turns.zh: 就在未来两年、三年内某个时候。5%，那大约是 1 万亿美元。作为对比，根据 Fed 的数据，整个美国银行体系的全部股权资本基础是 2.6 万亿美元。

turns.en: So every 5% default rate increase on consumer debt as a result of AI unemployment or deflation in wages, is equal to 40%, 40% of the total equity base of the United States banking system.
turns.zh: 所以，消费债务违约率每因 AI 造成的失业或工资通缩而上升 5%，就相当于美国银行体系总股权基础的 40%——40%。

turns.en: You see the problem here? And that's the side that no one's talking about yet. And I think they need to be. If 40% of the equity capital base, so what are banks gonna do if AI starts to create this joblessness?
turns.zh: 你看到这里的问题了吗？这就是那个还没有人在谈论的层面。而我认为他们需要开始谈。如果股权资本基础的 40% 受到冲击，那么当 AI 开始制造这种失业时，银行要怎么办？

turns.en: They can stop making loans. They can, you know, again, take this as the greatest, I'm a tourist, but they can stop making loans. They can sell treasuries that they're holding for as high quality liquid asset to raise capital.
turns.zh: 他们可以停止放贷。他们可以——你知道，还是把这当作一个外行人的说法，我只是个“游客”——他们可以停止放贷。他们可以卖出自己作为高质量流动性资产（HQLA）持有的国债来筹集资本。

turns.en: But oops, now you're gonna have another seller of treasuries to go alongside foreigners, to go alongside Scott Besant, et cetera. They can issue equity, which the market isn't gonna love if banks start issuing trillions of dollars of equity.
turns.zh: 但哎呀，现在你又要多出一个国债卖家，和外国人并列，和 Scott Bessent 等等并列。他们可以发行股票，而如果银行开始发行数万亿美元的股票，市场是不会喜欢的。

turns.en: Because, oh, by the way, that's somebody else who's gotta issue capital alongside Scott Besant, alongside AI. And now the banks, eugh, that's not good for risk.
turns.zh: 因为，哦，顺便说一句，那就是又一个必须和 Scott Bessent 并列、和 AI 并列去发行资本的人。现在再加上银行，呃，这对风险资产不是好事。

turns.en: Or you slow the economy down a whole bunch. But none of those are good outcomes. That doesn't work for our debt position. We have to grow out of our debt.
turns.zh: 或者你就让经济大幅放缓。但这些没有一个是好结果。那对我们的债务状况行不通。我们必须靠增长走出债务。

turns.en: When we slow down, we don't grow out of our debt. And so I think it's almost like, to me, the last two weeks, particularly around this Microsoft news.
turns.zh: 而当我们放缓的时候，我们就无法靠增长走出债务。所以我认为，这几乎就像——对我来说，过去两周，尤其是围绕 Microsoft 这条新闻。

turns.en: This Microsoft news, I think, was like the, we're gonna need a bigger boat moment for the employment argument around AI. And I think that's, I think some of what we're seeing with the topiness of the market that you're describing and the fact that bank stocks have rolled over and consumer credit has rolled over and Blackstone has rolled over and Blue Owl has rolled over, American Express, Capital One,
turns.zh: 这条 Microsoft 的新闻，我认为就像是关于 AI 的就业论点的那个“我们需要一艘更大的船”（we're gonna need a bigger boat）时刻。而我认为，这正是我们在你所描述的市场见顶迹象中看到的一部分：银行股已经掉头向下，消费信贷已经掉头向下，Blackstone 已经掉头向下，Blue Owl 已经掉头向下，American Express、Capital One、

turns.en: all these stocks, they've massively underperformed the S&P over the last three to six months. Why? If AI works, why would I want to own any of this stuff?
turns.zh: 所有这些股票，它们在过去三到六个月里大幅跑输标普 500（S&P 500）。为什么？如果 AI 有效，我为什么会想持有这些东西中的任何一个？

turns.en: Makes no sense. That, to me, is the more troubling thing. And it's the more, I wonder if that isn't starting to factor into the mind of the market of just this gigantic credit problem that we haven't even started discussing really publicly yet in a major way.
turns.zh: 完全说不通。对我来说，这才是更令人不安的事情。而我更怀疑，这是不是已经开始进入市场的思维：就是这么一个巨大的信贷问题，而我们甚至还没有真正开始以主要方式公开讨论它。

turns.en: We're still very focused on sort of the narrow tranche of, hey, can they keep blowing through a trillion dollars or $600 billion, whatever the ridiculous number is, a year in capital and as the rates go up because, you know, and we haven't even gotten to the consumer side of this, like, hey, if this actually works, we're gonna have a credit default cycle in consumer that makes a weight look like pretty tame.
turns.zh: 我们仍然非常聚焦于那个狭窄的切片：嘿，他们能不能继续每年烧掉 1 万亿美元或者 6000 亿美元——不管那个荒谬的数字是多少——的资本开支；而随着利率上升，因为我们甚至还没有触及这件事的消费端，就像，嘿，如果这东西真的有效，我们将在消费端迎来一轮信用违约周期，其严重程度会让以往任何一轮都显得相当温和。

turns.en: So that, it's kind of a ramble there. It's a thought stream, but that, to me, I think is starting to get, I know it factors into my mind. I'm managing my own money.
turns.zh: 所以，那里有点跑题了。这是一段思绪流，但对我来说，我认为它正在开始——我知道它已经进入了我的思维。我在管理我自己的钱。

turns.en: I'm sitting in 30% of my liquid net worth in cash and T-bills. Cause I look at this and I just go, like I don't like shorting stocks in a rig market where, you know, liquidity is provided to, you know, supply when it's needed because we're in fiscal dominance.
turns.zh: 我把流动净资产的 30% 放在现金和 T-bills（短期国库券）里。因为我看着这一切，我就想：我不喜欢在这样的市场里做空股票——在这个市场里，流动性会在需要的时候被提供出来，因为我们处在财政主导（fiscal dominance）之下。

turns.en: And, you know, so anytime the Treasury market asks, ugh, they're gonna step in and do something, but yikes, I don't know how this is gonna play out, but that's the fact that this isn't being talked about yet.
turns.zh: 而且，你知道，所以任何时候国债市场一出问题，呃，他们就会介入做点什么。但是天哪，我不知道这会怎么演变。可是“这件事还没有被讨论”这个事实，

turns.en: While some of these names are not acting great, makes me cautious. I'm trying to get my head around the policy response and particularly whether and to what extent it would matter or make a difference.
turns.zh: 而这些股票中的一些表现并不好，这让我保持谨慎。——我在试图弄清楚政策回应，尤其是如果这种 AI 资本开支繁荣真的开始瓦解，政策回应是否以及在多大程度上会重要、会带来差别。

turns.en: If we did see this AI capex boom start to fall apart because the Trump administration's been incredibly vocal saying dominance in AI and energy is kind of, you know, that's the whole thing for them.
turns.zh: 因为 Trump 政府一直在极其高调地说，在 AI 和能源上占据主导地位，就是他们的全部要义，

turns.en: That's their priority. You look at David Sacks in his role, basically telling anthropic to pound stand when they wanted to slow things down or regulate AI.
turns.zh: 那是他们的优先事项。你看看 David Sacks 在他的角色上，基本上是在 Anthropic 想要放慢脚步或者监管 AI 的时候叫他们一边去。

turns.en: We're not gonna regulate anything. It's full steam ahead. Okay, so let's imagine that we do see this capex boom starting to, you know, as rates back up, it runs out of steam and the ability of private credit to finance that continued AI capex spend starts to dry up.
turns.zh: “我们什么都不会监管。全速前进。”好，那么假设我们确实看到这个资本开支繁荣开始——你知道——随着利率回升而失去动力，而私人信贷为持续的 AI 资本开支提供融资的能力开始枯竭。

turns.en: Do we get a Trump administration policy response, which is all of a sudden there's a bunch of government money to bail out AI in order to keep it going in the name of national security?
turns.zh: 我们会不会看到 Trump 政府的政策回应，也就是突然冒出一大堆政府资金来救助 AI，以便以国家安全的名义让它继续下去？

turns.en: I mean, I could certainly see David Sacks advocating for that. What do you think? Is that, you know, if they wanted to push something like that, they'd probably need to do it before any change of power in the Congress, you know, after the midterm elections, we've still got a lame duck period until January.
turns.zh: 我是说，我完全能想象 David Sacks 会为此倡导。你怎么看？如果他们想推动这样的事情，他们可能需要在国会权力更迭之前做，你知道，中期选举之后我们还有一个到 1 月的跛脚鸭期（lame duck period）。

turns.en: You know, what could happen between now and January? Yeah, the Overton windows wide open. Yeah, I mean, Sacks said, hey, we don't want any regulation, blah, blah, blah.
turns.zh: 你知道，从现在到 1 月之间可能发生什么？——是的，奥弗顿窗口（Overton window）是完全敞开的。是的，我是说，Sacks 说“嘿，我们不要任何监管”，等等等等。

turns.en: And then his administration turned around and banned deep seek from any government programs and from any companies that sell into government programs.
turns.zh: 然后他的政府转头就把 DeepSeek 从所有政府项目中封禁了，也从所有向政府项目销售的公司中封禁了。

turns.en: So, and that's, look, I'm not naive as to why they did that. And that's a regulation, that's a moat that they helped try to put up around the economics of opening an anthropic.
turns.zh: 所以，这就是——听着，我对他们为什么这么做并不天真。那就是一项监管，那就是一道他们帮着试图围绕 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的经济性筑起的护城河。

turns.en: So Sacks, you know, whether Sacks had any say in that policy or not, I don't know, but the fact is he's a part of the administration and the administration put that in.
turns.zh: 所以 Sacks，你知道，Sacks 对那项政策有没有发言权，我不知道，但事实是他是这届政府的一员，而这届政府推出了那项政策。

turns.en: And so the administration at the very least made him a hypocrite because they did intervene to put a moat up under auspices of, hey, we need to keep the Chinese out of here, which might be the right thing to do, but that's a moat.
turns.zh: 所以这届政府至少把他变成了一个伪君子，因为他们确实出手干预了，以“嘿，我们需要把中国人挡在外面”的名义筑起了一道护城河——那可能是正确的事情，但那是一道护城河。

turns.en: Yeah, AI is now too big to fail. If, and I hear credible rumblings that subject was broached in Washington over a year ago. What happens if something happens?
turns.zh: 是的，AI 现在已经“大到不能倒”（too big to fail）了。而且我听到一些可信的传闻，说这个议题一年多以前就在华盛顿被提出过：如果出事了怎么办？

turns.en: How are we gonna step in? Will we step in? That was a subject that, you know, they began discussing contingency plans for, I hear. So if the credit mania bursts, then yeah, there's gonna be massive losses.
turns.zh: 我们要怎么介入？我们会介入吗？我听到说，那是一个他们开始讨论应急方案的议题。所以如果这场信贷狂热破裂，那么是的，会出现巨额损失。

turns.en: You're gonna have a recession because it's, you know, at least it's a big chunk of marginal growth in this country, unemployment will rise, and so they're gonna have to step up and do something because, you know, we're, even with this mania, US interest plus the entitlements and plus veterans affairs is running at 105% of receipts.
turns.zh: 你会迎来一场衰退，因为这——你知道——至少它是这个国家边际增长中的一大块。失业率会上升，所以他们将不得不站出来做点什么。因为你知道，即使有这场狂热，美国的利息支出加上权益类支出（entitlements）加上退伍军人事务部，已经达到了财政收入的 105%。

turns.en: And so if that mania bursts, receipts are gonna fall pretty sharply. And, you know, the offset might be a marginal respite for interest rates for a bit, right?
turns.zh: 所以如果那场狂热破裂，财政收入会相当急剧地下降。而且，你知道，抵消项可能是利率在一段时间内边际上的喘息，对吧？

turns.en: Because now all of a sudden maybe they wouldn't be competing with Besson to raise debt. And the amount of debt that Besson was gonna need to raise would need to go up by $400, $500 billion.
turns.zh: 因为现在突然之间，也许他们就不必和 Bessent 竞争发债了。而 Bessent 原本需要募集的债务规模将会需要增加 4000 亿、5000 亿美元。

turns.en: So nearly the entire amount that they're raising. Because if we had a recession, the deficit rises in this country last three, deficits gone up by 600 basis points, 800 basis points, and 1,000 basis points of GDP.
turns.zh: 所以差不多就是他们正在募集的全部金额。因为如果我们经历一场衰退，这个国家的赤字就会上升。过去三次，赤字分别上升了 GDP 的 600 个基点、800 个基点和 1000 个基点。

turns.en: 600 basis points, let's say 600 to 800, throughout the extreme case of COVID. 600, 800 basis points of GDP is 1.8 to 2.3. 4 trillion dollars.
turns.zh: 600 个基点，我们就说 600 到 800 个基点，贯穿 COVID 那个极端案例。GDP 的 600、800 个基点就是 1.8 万亿到 2.4 万亿美元。

turns.en: So that's how much more of the deficit's gonna go up in a recession. So we're running $2 trillion deficits today in a recession caused by a bursting of the AI mania very easily could add another $2 trillion deficit.
turns.zh: 所以这就是在一场衰退中赤字还会再增加多少。所以我们今天正在运行 2 万亿美元的赤字，而在一场由 AI 狂热破裂引发的衰退中，很容易再增加 2 万亿美元的赤字。

turns.en: So now you got a $4 trillion deficit. You gotta finance that extra $2 trillion. So I've seen people say, well, hey, if AI slows down, yields will really come down at the long end and Besson can issue there.
turns.zh: 所以你现在有了 4 万亿美元的赤字。你必须为那额外的 2 万亿美元融资。所以我看到有人说：嘿，如果 AI 放缓，长端收益率会真正下来，Bessent 就可以在那里发债。

turns.en: It was like, I think they'll come down for a second on sentiment and on that narrative. People will trade that narrative for a second. And then Besson will give his first QRA, his quarterly refunding announcement and go, hey guys, we thought we were gonna have to issue 2 trillion a year.
turns.zh: 我会想：我认为它们会因为情绪、因为那个叙事而下来一会儿。人们会交易那个叙事一小段时间。然后 Bessent 会给出他的第一次 QRA（季度再融资公告，Quarterly Refunding Announcement），然后说：嘿各位，我们原以为每年要发 2 万亿。

turns.en: It's actually closer to 3.5 trillion. And the long end will go, and that'll be that. That to me is, I don't know what to make of it other than like, I would fade the bond rally all day long because one way or another, someone's gonna borrow that money and the market's been demanding a higher rate.
turns.zh: 实际上更接近 3.5 万亿。然后长端就会崩，就这样。这对我来说——我不知道该怎么解读，只能说我会一整天都在做空债券反弹，因为不管以哪种方式，总有人要借那笔钱，而市场一直在要求更高的利率。

turns.en: So, you know, the one way I would not fade is if the Fed was involved or if Treasury is doing buybacks or they shifted a bunch to the short end, whatever.
turns.zh: 所以，你知道，唯一我不会去做空的情形是 Fed 参与其中，或者财政部在做回购，或者他们把大量发行转移到短端，诸如此类。

turns.en: But I don't know what the policy response would be because a recession is just not a policy option at all. Because, oh, by the way, right? We just said, in a recession, you could easily add 2 trillion dollars to our 2 trillion dollar deficit.
turns.zh: 但我不知道政策回应会是什么，因为衰退根本就不是一个政策选项。因为，哦，顺便说一句，对吧？我们刚刚说过，在一场衰退中，你很容易给我们 2 万亿美元的赤字再加上 2 万亿美元。

turns.en: So, we would have 4 trillion a year in issuance. That's bad enough. But now in a recession, remember what I just said about credit losses for the banks?
turns.zh: 所以我们每年的发行量会是 4 万亿。那已经够糟糕了。但现在在一场衰退中，还记得我刚才说的银行信贷损失吗？

turns.en: What are they gonna sell? To offset credit losses, Treasuries. Okay, so now they're joining Besson. So, whatever the, with 4 trillion dollars from Besson, we'll probably add 2, 300 billion a year from the banks in Treasury selling.
turns.zh: 他们要卖什么来抵消信贷损失？国债。好，所以现在他们加入了 Bessent 的行列。所以，不管怎么样，Bessent 那边 4 万亿美元，我们大概还会从银行的国债抛售中每年再加上 2000、3000 亿美元。

turns.en: Now we're at 4.3 trillion dollars. Dollar's gonna rise in a recession, as it always does. Dollar was up this year. Foreign central banks are on pace to sell almost 600 billion dollars since February in Treasuries.
turns.zh: 现在我们是 4.3 万亿美元。美元在一场衰退中会升值，就像它一贯的那样。今年美元是涨的。外国央行自 2 月以来，抛售国债的节奏接近 6000 亿美元。

turns.en: Foreign central banks. Throw another 600 billion on top of that. We're up to almost 5 trillion in effective deficits. Now let's factor in the fact that 8% of the Treasury market is owned by hedge funds.
turns.zh: 外国央行。再往上面加 6000 亿。我们就到了接近 5 万亿美元的有效赤字。现在再把一个事实考虑进来：国债市场有 8% 由对冲基金持有。

turns.en: How do they came in? They're not gonna be grossing up into a recession. They're gonna be de-grossing everything, including Treasury. So, let's say they sell another, I don't know, $200 billion worth of Treasuries.
turns.zh: 他们是怎么进来的？他们不会在一场衰退中加杠杆扩张（grossing up）。他们会去杠杆（de-grossing）所有东西，包括国债。所以，就说他们再卖出——我不知道——2000 亿美元的国债。

turns.en: We're at 5.1, $5.2 trillion worth of Treasury supply. And who's the buyer? Mom and Pop? Is there losing their jobs? Pensions? Is there paying out early withdrawals who are also a big owner of Treasuries?
turns.zh: 我们就到了 5.1、5.2 万亿美元的国债供给。而买家是谁？是正在失去工作的普通散户（Mom and Pop）？是正在支付提前支取的养老金——他们也是国债的大持有人？

turns.en: No, there's only one buyer. It's the Fed. Fed's gonna have to print money and buy Treasuries, and they will say, we're not monetizing the debt, and we're not monetizing the, then it'll all be bull crap.
turns.zh: 不，只有一个买家，那就是 Fed。Fed 将不得不印钞买国债，然后他们会说“我们不是在债务货币化，我们不是在货币化”，然后这一切都将是一派胡言。

turns.en: That's okay. But that can't happen. That policy response we talk about, that can't happen until you have a crisis. Because otherwise, it's just handouts for the banks.
turns.zh: 没关系。但那不能发生。我们谈论的那个政策回应，在你先有一场危机之前是不能发生的。因为否则那就只是给银行的施舍。

turns.en: You gotta scare people first. See, the thing is, I think there is a very realistic setup for a crisis, and the analogy I would use is the 2000.com bust.
turns.zh: 你得先把人吓到。——你看，事情是这样的，我认为存在一个非常现实的危机形成条件，而我会用的类比是 2000 年互联网泡沫（dot-com bust）的破裂。

turns.en: And look, the bet that was being made there was a correct bet. Everybody thought the internet was gonna be a really big deal, and they were right in that call.
turns.zh: 而且你看，当时下的那个赌注是一个正确的赌注。所有人都认为互联网将会是一件非常大的事，而他们在那个判断上是对的。

turns.en: But the thing is, the market got ahead of itself. And we just had too much malinvestment in all the wrong.coms. What you've got now is this massive credit-driven spend out on AI.
turns.zh: 但问题在于，市场跑到了自己前面。我们在所有的 .com 公司上有了太多错误的投资（malinvestment）。而你现在拥有的是这一大笔由信贷驱动的 AI 支出。

turns.en: And it is giving the US Frontier Labs the lead. But as Matt Barry has pointed out on this program, only a lead by six months or so. China is not very far behind.
turns.zh: 而它正在让美国的前沿实验室（Frontier Labs）取得领先。但正如 Matt Barry 在本节目上指出的，只是领先六个月左右而已。中国并没有落后很多。

turns.en: And that means if we had a credit bust in AI, it would legitimately risk China taking over and basically becoming the dominant power in AI globally.
turns.zh: 而这意味着，如果我们在 AI 上出现信贷破裂，它将确实带来中国接管、并基本上成为全球 AI 主导力量的风险。

turns.en: And that really is a genuine national security risk, in my opinion. Okay, you know what Besant is gonna say to that. The answer is no. From a policy standpoint, we will not allow that to happen on my watch.
turns.zh: 而在我看来，那是一个真正的国家安全风险。——好，你知道 Bessent 对此会说什么。答案是“不”。从政策立场来说，我们不会允许这种事情在我的任期内发生。

turns.en: Okay, he's probably willing, it's not like Besant is a guy who's sheepish about taking bold policy moves. So, I mean, there could be almost any policy response to stop an AI bubble from bursting.
turns.zh: 好，他大概是愿意这么做的，Bessent 不是一个在采取大胆政策行动上畏首畏尾的人。所以，我是说，几乎任何政策回应都可能被用来阻止 AI 泡沫破裂。

turns.en: Okay, how is that going to be received politically as we get into what could be a lame duck session where maybe even both houses of Congress have been taken by the Democrats, but they haven't taken office yet.
turns.zh: 好，那么当我们进入一个可能的跛脚鸭会期时——也许届时国会两院都已被民主党拿下，但他们还没有上任——这在政治上会如何被接受？

turns.en: And Besant's trying to move policy actions through Congress before the lame duck session ends. And then meanwhile, on top of all this, now Luke, I don't usually, I'm not one of these guys who picks through S1 statements trying to find little risks where they have to disclose, you know, we're city bank and if there's gonna be a new online form of credit, maybe it poses a risk to our business.
turns.zh: 而且 Bessent 正试图在跛脚鸭会期结束之前，通过国会推动政策行动。然后与此同时，在所有这些之上，现在 Luke，我通常不是那种翻 S-1 招股说明书（S-1）去找小风险的人——就是那种他们必须披露的地方，你知道，“我们是 Citibank，如果出现一种新的线上信贷形式，也许它会对我们的业务构成风险”。

turns.en: But here's a direct quote from Anthropics S1 just filed for their IPO. Concerns have been raised both within our organization by other researchers, regulators, policy makers, and industry participants that sufficiently advanced AI systems could, if not developed, deployed, and operated with an appropriate safeguards, oversight, and security measures, pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity.
turns.zh: 但这里有一段来自 Anthropic 为 IPO 刚刚提交的 S-1 的直接引文：“我们组织内部的其他研究人员、监管机构、政策制定者和行业参与者都曾提出担忧：充分先进的 AI 系统，如果在开发、部署和运营时没有适当的安全护栏、监督和安全措施，可能对人类构成灾难性或存在性风险。”

turns.en: Okay, I'm pretty sure there's never been an S1 statement filed with the SEC before that says, oh, by the way, in terms of just minor things that could go wrong that you might wanna look at in terms of reviewing our IPO, our stuff could end humanity.
turns.zh: 好，我相当确定，以前从来没有一份提交给 SEC 的 S-1 里写过：哦，顺便说一句，在一些你可能想在审核我们 IPO 时看一眼的小问题方面，我们的东西可能终结人类。

turns.en: I don't think anybody ever said that in an S1 before. So if you were trying, if you're thinking about how a setup could come together for a really strong left versus right, Democrat versus Republican, you got Scott Besant and David Sacks probably saying we can not allow the AI boom to stop.
turns.zh: 我不认为以前有人在 S-1 里这么写过。所以如果你在试图思考一个局面如何能够形成——一场真正强烈的左对右、民主党对共和党的对峙——你这边有 Scott Bessent 和 David Sacks，他们大概在说：我们不能允许 AI 繁荣停下来。

turns.en: It is a matter of national security. It must be supported no matter what. Who could possibly give the Democrats better ammunition than this S1 statement?
turns.zh: 这是国家安全问题。无论如何都必须得到支持。那么还有谁能给民主党提供更好的弹药，比这份 S-1 声明更好？

turns.en: This is, oh, by the way, it risks humanity, the existential threat to humanity. That's bigger than Besant's claim of a massive economic crash.
turns.zh: 这就是——哦，顺便说一句，它危及人类，是对人类的存在性威胁。这比 Bessent 所说的“大规模经济崩溃”还要大。

turns.en: How does that get litigated between the midterms and the actual handing over of power on January 21st? What is the forest for the trees? I'll look on that one.
turns.zh: 这件事在中期选举和 1 月 21 日实际权力交接之间会如何被博弈？Forrest for the Trees 对此的看法是什么？

turns.en: It reminds me of that cartoon. There's a cartoon that's like, you know, three people sitting around a fire in rags saying, you know, we ended up destroying the earth, but for a moment there, we really created some shareholder value.
turns.zh: 这让我想起那幅漫画。有一幅漫画是这样的：你知道，三个人衣衫褴褛地围坐在火堆旁说：“你知道，我们最终毁掉了地球，但在那一瞬间，我们确实创造了一些股东价值。”

turns.en: And I don't know how it gets litigated between election day and when people are sworn into their new seats. The thing that keeps sticking out in my head or the splinter in my brain about all of this or one of the splinters in my brain about all this is that even if Besant and Sack say, we're not gonna let that happen and they stop it, I wonder if it's a booby prize, which is to say by luck of the draw or whatever,
turns.zh: 而我不知道这件事在选举日和新人宣誓就职之间会如何被博弈。这件事一直卡在我脑子里——或者说关于这一切我脑子里的刺，或者说其中一根刺——是：即使 Bessent 和 Sacks 说“我们不会让那发生”并且他们阻止了它，我怀疑那会不会是一个安慰奖（booby prize）。也就是说，凭运气或者别的什么，

turns.en: China's one child policy means they have a catastrophic demographic problem. Ask any China hawk, any China bear about it. China is screwed because their demographics are shrinking.
turns.zh: 中国的独生子女政策意味着他们有一个灾难性的人口结构问题。你去问任何一位中国鹰派、任何一位中国空头，都是这个说法：中国完蛋了，因为他们的人口在萎缩。

turns.en: And yet, if AI actually does what it says it's gonna do and Besant and Sack's at all won't let it fail even if it would collapse under its own weight, and America, unlike China, does not have a catastrophic demographic issue in the traditional sense of the word.
turns.zh: 然而，如果 AI 真的做到了它声称要做的事情，而 Bessent 和 Sacks 又绝不肯让它失败——即便它会因为自身重量而崩塌——并且美国与中国不同，在传统意义上并没有灾难性的人口问题。

turns.en: We have a growing population, very heterogeneous population that can barely get along as we speak today. And now you're gonna start whacking people's jobs in five and 10 and in Microsoft's point 27% chunks.
turns.zh: 我们有一个不断增长的人口、非常异质化的人口，即便在今天也几乎无法和睦相处。而现在你要开始以 5%、10%，以 Microsoft 那样的 27% 的规模砍掉人们的工作。

turns.en: In the meantime, over in China and Japan and Korea, with their catastrophic demographics, they're still gonna get hurt by AI taking jobs so fast, but they're homogenous cultures with rapidly shrinking populations.
turns.zh: 与此同时，在中国、日本、韩国，那些有着灾难性人口结构的国家，他们仍然会因为 AI 太快夺走工作而受伤，但他们是同质文化、人口迅速萎缩。

turns.en: And I look at this and go, I know what happens to cultures with very heterogeneous growing populations and not enough jobs. Google France, Google Middle East, right?
turns.zh: 而我看着这一切，心想：我知道那些人口非常异质、不断增长而工作不够的社会会发生什么。搜一下法国（Google France），搜一下中东（Google Middle East），对吧？

turns.en: You can see how this is gonna go. And so that's why I say even if Sack's and Besant say this isn't gonna be allowed to happen and they succeed, which they very well, they probably are saying that, and they very well, probably will succeed, what will they win?
turns.zh: 你能看出这会怎么发展。所以这就是为什么我说，即使 Sacks 和 Bessent 说这不会被允许发生，而且他们成功了——他们很可能确实在这么说，也很可能确实会成功——他们赢到的是什么？

turns.en: Show them what they won, Bob. Here's the next five years of social unrest in the United States. And maybe that's what all the flock cameras are for.
turns.zh: 把他们赢到的东西拿给他们看看吧，Bob。这是接下来五年美国的社会动荡。也许这就是那些 Flock 摄像头是干什么用的。

turns.en: Maybe that's what Palantir's for. Maybe that's what all this is. And now we start to get to a really kind of dark place, but that's why I look at this and kind of go, I really wish there were more second and third derivative thinkers around this administration rather than sort of like the obvious move that's right in front of you.
turns.zh: 也许这就是 Palantir 是干什么用的。也许这一切就是干这个的。而现在我们开始进入一个相当黑暗的地方。但这就是为什么我看着这一切，然后想：我真的希望这届政府周围有更多做二阶、三阶思考的人，而不是那种就在你眼前的显而易见的一步。

turns.en: And some of that's a nature of our politics and some of it's a nature of our culture, but it is what it is. And that's, I look at this and go, when will this be litigated?
turns.zh: 其中一部分是我们政治的性质，一部分是我们文化的性质，但事实就是如此。而这——我看着这一切就想：这件事什么时候会被博弈？

turns.en: I don't know if it'll be litigated between November and January, but if AI does what I think it's gonna do, I think it's gonna start getting litigated in 2027.
turns.zh: 我不知道它会不会在 11 月到 1 月之间被博弈，但如果 AI 做到了我认为它会做到的事情，我认为它会在 2027 年开始被博弈。

turns.en: And how do I think it's gonna get litigated? I think it's gonna get litigated with model top cocktails in city centers around the United States, just like it's getting litigated in France right now, just like it's been getting litigated in the Middle East for decades.
turns.zh: 而我认为它会怎么被博弈？我认为它会以美国各地市中心里的莫洛托夫鸡尾酒（Molotov cocktails，燃烧瓶）来被博弈，就像它现在正在法国被博弈一样，就像它几十年来一直在中东被博弈一样。

turns.en: And it's an unpleasant thought, and I'm sure I'll get plenty of, oh, you're such a doomer, Luke, but this is just critical thinking. I'm sorry.
turns.zh: 这是一个不愉快的想法，我确信我会收到一大堆“哦，Luke 你真是个末日论者”。但这只是批判性思维。抱歉。

turns.en: If you're gonna start importing lots and lots of people to have a growing population and it's heterogeneous culture, and then you start whacking the good jobs out, you would have to be a moron who doesn't read history to understand how that's gonna go.
turns.zh: 如果你要开始进口大量人口以维持人口增长、而且是异质文化，然后你又开始砍掉那些好工作，你得多蠢、多不读历史，才会不明白那会怎么发展。

turns.en: Pick up Peter Turchin's book The End Times. Elite overproduction plus massive wealth inequality, it always ends the same way, always. So that's when I think it'll get litigated.
turns.zh: 去读 Peter Turchin 的书《End Times》。精英过度生产（elite overproduction）加上极端的财富不平等，结局永远是一样的，永远。所以那就是我认为它会被博弈的时候。

turns.en: It'll start to get litigated in 2027 in accelerating political instability in the West and in the United States as AI does all of this. Well, and I certainly think there's room to expect a pretty interesting presidential debate in 2028, but we don't wanna jump ahead of ourselves too much.
turns.zh: 它会从 2027 年开始被博弈，表现为西方以及美国加速的政治不稳定，因为 AI 做了所有这些事情。——嗯，而且我当然认为，有理由预期 2028 年会有一场相当有意思的总统辩论，但我们不想太超前。

turns.en: Luke, as always, I can't thank you enough for another terrific interview. I always really enjoy our talks, but before I let you go, please tell our listeners what you do at forestforthetrees.com and what people can expect to find when they visit fftt-llc.com.
turns.zh: Luke，一如既往，我无法充分感谢你带来的又一场精彩访谈。我一直非常享受我们的对谈。但在放你走之前，请告诉我们的听众你在 forestforthetrees.com 做什么，以及人们访问 fftt-llc.com 时能找到什么。

turns.en: Yeah, thanks, Eric. We aggregate a large amount of publicly available data in a unique manner trying to do, identify developing economic bottlenecks to help our clients make money.
turns.zh: 好的，谢谢 Eric。我们以一种独特的方式汇集大量公开可得的数据，试图识别正在形成的经济瓶颈，以帮助我们的客户赚钱。

turns.en: And if they wanna learn more about how we do that, et cetera, then go to fftt-llc.com for more information or check us out at x at Luke Groman, L-U-K-E-G-R-O-M-E-N.
turns.zh: 如果他们想了解更多关于我们是怎么做的等等，请访问 fftt-llc.com 获取更多信息，或者在 X 上关注我们：@Luke Gromen，L-U-K-E-G-R-O-M-E-N。

turns.en: And now it's time to bring Patrick and Missile in for our Macrovoices Market Desk. Patrick, where's the trade? Well, thanks, Eric. Luke's argument raises a credit risk that extends beyond the company's financing, the AI boom.
turns.zh: 现在是时候把 Patrick 和 Michelle 请进来，做我们的 MacroVoices Market Desk 环节了。Patrick，交易机会在哪里？——好的，谢谢 Eric。Luke 的论点提出了一个超出企业融资层面的信用风险，也就是 AI 繁荣背后的信用风险。

turns.en: If AI displaces workers and reduces their earning power, then the outstanding debt still need to be serviced. Productivity gains for businesses could therefore come with deteriorating credit quality for consumer lenders.
turns.zh: 如果 AI 取代了工人、削弱了他们的收入能力，那么那些未偿债务仍然需要被偿付。因此，企业端的生产率提升，可能伴随着消费信贷机构信用质量的恶化。

turns.en: Capital One's exposure to credit cards and auto lending makes it a candidate for expressing that concern. The technical backdrop adds to the case.
turns.zh: Capital One 在信用卡和汽车贷款上的敞口，使它成为表达这一担忧的候选标的。技术面的背景也加强了这个逻辑。

turns.en: The stock peaked back in January and has spent much of the year under pressure. Following earnings, it's pivoting at its 50-day moving average.
turns.zh: 该股在 1 月见顶，一年中大部分时间都承受压力。财报之后，它正在 50 日均线附近徘徊。

turns.en: A failure around this level would reinforce the bearer structure and leave the stock vulnerable for another leg lower. With Capital One, symbol COF, trading around $204.88, I'm looking at the January 15th, 2027.
turns.zh: 在这一位置失守将强化看跌结构，并让该股面临再下一个台阶的风险。Capital One，代码 COF，交易价格约为 204.88 美元，我看的是 2027 年 1 月 15 日到期的

turns.en: 200 by 175 bear put spread, trading around $5.96 net debit. The $25 spread offers a maximum profit of $19.04 per share against that $5.96 commitment, giving it approximately a three-to-one risk-reward ratio.
turns.zh: 200 乘 175 熊市看跌价差（bear put spread），净支出约为 5.96 美元。这个 25 美元的价差提供每股最高 19.04 美元的利润，对应 5.96 美元的投入，风险回报比大约是三比一。

turns.en: Now, with the implied volatility on Capital One near the bottom of its one-year range, owning even the January 200 put outright for $7.95 is also a reasonable alternative for seeking greater downside participation.
turns.zh: 另外，由于 Capital One 的隐含波动率（implied volatility）接近其一年区间底部，直接以 7.95 美元买入 1 月 200 行权价的看跌期权，也是寻求更大下行参与的合理替代方案。

turns.en: We're expressing a specific vulnerability in consumer credit through a stock already showing technical weakness with a defined capital commitment and more than $3 of profit potential for every $1 risk.
turns.zh: 我们是在通过一只已经显示出技术面疲弱的股票，来表达消费信贷中的一个特定脆弱点，资本投入是确定的，而每承担 1 美元风险有超过 3 美元的潜在利润。

turns.en: That's where's the trade. Patrick analyzes and trades the markets every day over at Big Picture Trading. Macrovoices listeners can sign up for a free two-week trial at bigpicturetrading.com.
turns.zh: 这就是“交易机会在哪里”（Where's the Trade）。Patrick 每天都在 Big Picture Trading 分析和交易市场。MacroVoices 的听众可以在 bigpicturetrading.com 注册，获得两周免费试用。

turns.en: Now back to Patrick and Maseel. All right, Patrick, we've had the Fed announced no rate hike yesterday and there's a huge round of big tech earnings this week, but what set out to you the most?
turns.zh: 现在回到 Patrick 和 Michelle。——好的，Patrick，Fed 昨天宣布不加息，本周又有一大批大型科技股财报，但最让你在意的是什么？

turns.en: Let's start off with talking about the mixed earnings reaction. Microsoft higher, Alphabet sharply lower and no convincing bullish impulse across the market.
turns.zh: 我们先从财报反应分化说起。Microsoft 上涨，Alphabet 大幅下跌，整个市场没有出现有说服力的看多动能。

turns.en: The AI spending cash flow is now under scrutiny. Microsoft's quarterly free cash flow was like $18 billion versus Alphabet minus $9 billion.
turns.zh: AI 支出的现金流现在开始受到审视。Microsoft 的季度自由现金流大约是 180 亿美元，而 Alphabet 是负 90 亿美元。

turns.en: Growing distinction between funding the build out versus delivering returns. Now, particularly with Microsoft, we wanna really see whether it can follow through.
turns.zh: 在为建设融资与交付回报之间，出现了越来越明显的区别。现在，特别是对于 Microsoft，我们真正想看的是它能不能有后续跟进。

turns.en: That's gonna be the big test. It's now approaching its previous high. Will it retreat and will the big money sell into the strength or will there be genuine follow through?
turns.zh: 那将是重大考验。它现在正在逼近前高。它会回落吗？大资金会趁着强势卖出吗？还是会有真正的跟进上涨？

turns.en: It's gonna be a really big tell. At the same time, Google with this gap down has really solidified a very clear downtrend and it will be pretty hard for it to recover immediately.
turns.zh: 这将是一个非常重大的信号。同时，Google 这次向下跳空，已经确立了一个非常清晰的下跌趋势，它将很难立即恢复。

turns.en: Now, the NASDAQ is now below its 50 day moving average in what is essentially a bear flag. And we were looking to see whether any of these MAG7s could meaningfully turn the entire NASDAQ trend back bullishly.
turns.zh: 现在，纳斯达克（NASDAQ）已经跌破其 50 日均线，本质上是一个熊旗（bear flag）。而我们一直在观察，这些 MAG7（七巨头）中是否有任何一只能够有意义地把整个纳斯达克趋势重新扭转回多头。

turns.en: There's no sign of that yet. Now, the S&P 500 continues to trade above the critical levels around 76 to 7700 where there's a number of systematic sell zones where we would see CTAs and vol targeting funds and other things potentially start to unwind their strong bullish positioning.
turns.zh: 目前还没有这样的迹象。现在，标普 500（S&P 500）继续在 7600 到 7700 附近的关键水平上方交易，那里有一系列系统性卖出区间，我们可能会看到 CTA、波动率目标基金（vol targeting funds）以及其他资金开始解除它们强烈的多头仓位。

turns.en: Now, overall, even though the market's breath has been improving, this really does continue to be a MAG7 story. They remain a 35% waiting in the S&P 500 and have been the core part of the market that has been able to maintain this bold trend with the MAG7 basket now trading at its 50 day moving average.
turns.zh: 现在，总体来看，即便市场广度一直在改善，这仍然是一个 MAG7 的故事。它们在标普 500 中的权重仍约为 35%，一直是市场核心中能够维持这一多头趋势的部分，而 MAG7 一篮子股票现在正好交易在其 50 日均线上。

turns.en: The big question here is that did Google somehow take the wind out of the sales of this MAG7 basket? And are we seeing the beginning of a little bit of distribution here?
turns.zh: 这里的大问题是：Google 是不是在某种程度上抽走了 MAG7 这一篮子股票涨势的动能？我们是不是正在看到一点点派发（distribution）的开始？

turns.en: I think it's going to play an critical component as to whether the S&P is going to be able to hold above those key levels. OK, but what did you take from the Fed's message yesterday?
turns.zh: 我认为这将在标普能否守住那些关键水平上扮演一个关键角色。——好，那么你怎么看 Fed 昨天传达的信息？

turns.en: Well, the market was expecting a hawkish hold, and they got it. It was a bit of a softer press conference in terms of the tone. But overall, when you look at the actual reactions of the market to the FOMC, then pretty much the market got what they were expecting because there was no real big surprise or move in the repricing of any of the assets.
turns.zh: 嗯，市场原本预期一次鹰派的按兵不动，而他们得到了。就语气而言，新闻发布会稍微温和了一些。但总体来看，当你观察市场对 FOMC 的实际反应时，市场基本上得到了他们预期的东西，因为没有任何真正的重大意外，也没有任何资产重新定价上的大动作。

turns.en: Now, what was interesting, well, Warsh did acknowledge some tightening of financial conditions, fell short of calling it actually tight, and no declaration that the bond markets have already done enough tightening.
turns.zh: 现在，有意思的是，Warsh 确实承认金融条件有所收紧，但没有说到实际上已经“紧”的程度，也没有宣称债券市场已经完成了足够的紧缩。

turns.en: And so what is the overall response? Well, surprisingly, the SOFR and short term Treasury bond yields are relatively unchanged in the reaction.
turns.zh: 那么整体反应是什么？嗯，令人意外的是，SOFR 和短期国债收益率在反应中基本没有变化。

turns.en: And even the longer duration bonds, like the 10 and 30 year, have stayed within the range of the previous week. So from a response, the Fed basically gave the market what they priced in, and there are no immediate reactions.
turns.zh: 即使是更长期限的债券，比如 10 年期和 30 年期，也仍停留在前一周的区间内。所以从反应来看，Fed 基本上给了市场他们已经定价的东西，没有即时的反应。

turns.en: I think other parts of the macro space, like what oil does next are now going to play a much more pivotal role in the week to come. And now when looking at the dollar, did the Fed change anything meaningful?
turns.zh: 我认为宏观领域的其他部分，比如原油接下来怎么走，将在未来一周扮演更加关键的角色。——那么现在看美元，Fed 改变了什么有意义的东西吗？

turns.en: Well, really the dollar trend would have reversed if there was a dovish pivot, and there wasn't. So at this moment, the prevailing bull trend in the dollar remains intact, but the one currency pair to completely focus on is the euro.
turns.zh: 嗯，如果出现了鸽派转向，美元趋势本来会反转，但并没有出现。所以在这一刻，美元盛行的上升趋势依然完好，但需要完全聚焦的一个货币对是欧元。

turns.en: While we've seen in the pound and the Canadian dollar and the Aussie all have bounced and retraced a lot of their weakness, the euro remains along its 52 week lows.
turns.zh: 我们看到英镑、加元和澳元都已经反弹并回撤了很大一部分跌幅，而欧元仍然贴着它的 52 周低点。

turns.en: And if this one 11 level gives out, the euro may be starting another leg down. And because the euro is such a huge weighting in the dollar index, that alone may drive dollar strength, even without the dollar rising on funding stresses.
turns.zh: 而如果 1.11 这个水平失守，欧元可能开始新一轮下跌。而由于欧元在美元指数中的权重如此之大，仅这一点就可能推动美元走强，即便美元并没有因为融资压力而上涨。

turns.en: And so certainly a very interesting setup here. Overall, the US dollar bull trend remains intact, but increasingly, it really is the euro that we just have to watch.
turns.zh: 所以这肯定是一个非常有趣的局面。总体来看，美元的上升趋势依然完好，但越来越明显的是，我们真正需要盯住的是欧元。

turns.en: All right, Patrick, we have to turn to oil right now because we keep seeing flows coming in and buyers keep coming in to hold the asset. What are you specifically watching here?
turns.zh: 好的，Patrick，我们现在必须转向原油，因为我们不断看到资金流入、买家不断进场来持有这个资产。你具体在这里关注什么？

turns.en: Well, the key observation to make is that every piece headline we get, there's only a modest price response and almost always oil regains itself back to its previous highs in any reasonable period afterwards.
turns.zh: 嗯，需要做出的关键观察是：每当我们得到一条突发新闻，价格的反应都只是适度的，而且几乎总是在之后任何合理的时间段内，原油都会重新回到前高。

turns.en: So we continue to have an environment where oil is trending higher and very likely anticipating a re-escalation of the situation in the post midterm period.
turns.zh: 所以我们持续处在这样一个环境中：原油正在走高，并且很可能在预期中期选举之后局势的再度升级。

turns.en: At this moment, crude oil remains in a decisive bull trend and it would take some sort of a geopolitical disruption at this point to disrupt this trend.
turns.zh: 在这一刻，原油仍处在一个决定性的上升趋势中，而在当前这个节点，需要某种地缘政治冲击才能打破这一趋势。

turns.en: And so at this stage, a technical upside is back to the $120 previous highs on WTI and Brent could certainly clear the previous highs if that was underway.
turns.zh: 所以在这个阶段，技术面的上行目标是回到 WTI 和 Brent 之前 120 美元的高点，如果那种情况正在发生，它们完全可能突破前高。

turns.en: All right, now when we turn to gold, it's trading at a key psychological level right at $4,000. What would it need for the asset to trade higher or break lower?
turns.zh: 好的，那么现在转向黄金，它正交易在 4000 美元这个关键心理关口上。这个资产要向上交易或者向下突破，需要什么条件？

turns.en: Well, gold really needed a dovish pivot from the Fed and some sort of a change in the macro backdrop and that just didn't happen. At this moment, gold is trading along its $4,000 support line where we're the lows of the summer and there is simply no accumulation happening whatsoever.
turns.zh: 嗯，黄金真正需要的是 Fed 的鸽派转向，以及宏观背景的某种改变，而那并没有发生。在这一刻，黄金正沿着其 4000 美元的支撑线交易，那里是我们夏季的低点所在，而且完全没有出现任何吸筹（accumulation）。

turns.en: It's a distributive chart and there's no sign of buyers anywhere. At this moment, the prevailing downtrend is the one that's the path of least resistance and without an immediate catalyst, gold remains at a risk of a breakdown because a key technical breakdown like this would leave room for even a 5% to 10% further drawdown.
turns.zh: 这是一张派发（distributive）的图表，任何地方都看不到买家的迹象。在这一刻，盛行的下行趋势才是阻力最小的路径，而在没有立即出现的催化剂的情况下，黄金仍然面临跌破的风险，因为像这样的关键技术位跌破，会为进一步 5% 到 10% 的回撤留出空间。

turns.en: Overall, I remain very bullish gold long-term but on the short term, there is clearly a distribution cycle underway driven by macro catalysts and it's just a matter now of waiting out to see how the dust settles and when the actual inflection point or turn point on the gold trend materializes.
turns.zh: 总体来看，我对黄金长期仍然非常看多，但短期而言，显然有一轮由宏观催化剂驱动的派发周期正在进行，而现在只是等待尘埃落定，等待黄金趋势上真正的拐点或转向点出现。

turns.en: All right, let's turn to copper right now because we keep seeing distributive price action and top information, but what are you seeing in the charts?
turns.zh: 好的，那么现在转向铜，因为我们不断看到派发式的价格走势和顶部信息，但你在图表上看到的是什么？

turns.en: Going back a month or more, copper was the most bullish commodity out there in terms of positioning based on commitment of trader reports. Everyone was decisively bullish and there was a fundamental reason behind it but what's interesting is that over the last three months, copper has failed to break to a higher high and reward that bullish positioning.
turns.zh: 回溯一个月甚至更久，铜曾经是市场上最看多的商品——从交易者持仓报告（Commitment of Traders，COT）所反映的仓位来看。所有人都决定性地看多，而且背后有基本面的理由。但有意思的是，在过去三个月里，铜一直没能突破到更高的高点来回报那些多头仓位。

turns.en: Now we've seen some deterioration in the price and just now bouncing back to the 670 level near its 50 day moving average. This is an important moment where we're going to find out whether or not the bulls can neutralize this weakness and get this back up to the 52 week highs to set up a breakout, but right now with the way the price action is deteriorating, any breakdown below 650 could squeeze out
turns.zh: 现在我们看到价格出现了一些恶化，刚刚反弹回 670 这个水平，接近其 50 日均线。这是一个重要时刻，我们将看到多头能否中和这种疲弱，把价格重新推回 52 周高点，从而为突破创造条件。但就目前价格走势恶化的方式来看，任何跌破 650 都可能挤出

turns.en: the very crowded trade. At this moment, I would remain relatively neutral copper until we see some sort of technical price action showing some meaningful accumulation.
turns.zh: 那个非常拥挤的交易。在这一刻，我会对铜保持相对中性，直到我们看到某种技术面价格行为显示出有意义的吸筹。

turns.en: All right, when looking at the bigger spectrum of equities, stocks, commodities, was there anything else on your screens worth highlighting?
turns.zh: 好的，那么从更大范围来看——股票、大宗商品——你的屏幕上还有什么其他值得强调的东西吗？

turns.en: Well, I want to highlight the uranium disconnect because the U308 is trading around 91.30 a pound, holding well above $90, but at the same time, the equities remain in a decisive downtrend and continue to be hurt considerably.
turns.zh: 嗯，我想强调铀的背离，因为 U3O8 交易价格在每磅 91.30 美元左右，稳稳站在 90 美元上方，但与此同时，铀矿股票仍处于决定性的下跌趋势中，并持续受到相当大的伤害。

turns.en: Clearly, those uranium equities have been dragged down with a lot of the AI selling that has been going on. It will be interesting to see when these uranium equities finally can start banging out short-term lows and whether that ends up being a critical buying opportunity.
turns.zh: 显然，这些铀矿股票被大量正在发生的 AI 抛售拖累了。有意思的是要看这些铀矿股什么时候终于能开始砸出短期低点，以及那最终会不会成为一个关键的买入机会。

turns.en: Also worth noting is what's been happening in Brazil. Clearly, there was a huge shocker. Everyone was expecting Bolsonaro to win and that was being priced into this market.
turns.zh: 另外值得注意的是巴西正在发生的事情。显然，那是一个巨大的意外。所有人都预期 Bolsonaro 会赢，而那已经被定价进了这个市场。

turns.en: At this moment, we saw a huge gap in the 20 to 30% level on the downside in reaction to the election results and the question now is, was this one big buying opportunity or is there still further weakness to come?
turns.zh: 在这一刻，我们看到对选举结果的反应是向下跳空了 20% 到 30%，而现在的问题是：这是一个巨大的买入机会，还是仍有进一步的疲弱要来？

turns.en: Overall, we've seen price stability over the last couple of days. Will we have a full recovery back to like the 37 or 38 level on the EWZ, which is the Brazil ETF?
turns.zh: 总体来看，过去几天我们看到了价格的稳定。我们会不会看到完全回升到 EWZ——也就是巴西 ETF——37 或 38 那个水平？

turns.en: Certainly one of the more lively markets in this environment. All right, and what are the key things to watch from here? To me, it remains about earnings.
turns.zh: 这肯定是当前环境中较为活跃的市场之一。——好的，那么接下来要关注的关键事项是什么？——对我来说，仍然是财报。

turns.en: Not only do we have Amazon coming up and Apple next week, but with this asking questions like, will Microsoft hold these gains or we will find it giving them all back in the next couple of trading sessions?
turns.zh: 不仅下周有 Amazon 和 Apple，而且要问的问题是：Microsoft 会守住这些涨幅吗，还是我们会在接下来的几个交易日里看到它把涨幅全部回吐？

turns.en: Will Alphabet find support? There's so many big questions, but the Mag7 remain the focal point. Can the Mag7 bullishly resolve themselves in the post-earnings period because they are that important to the indices and what happens next in the S&P and the NASDAQ are really hinging on this?
turns.zh: Alphabet 会找到支撑吗？有太多重大问题了，但 MAG7 仍然是焦点。MAG7 能否在财报季后以多头方式解决问题？因为它们对指数就是这么重要，而标普和纳斯达克接下来会发生什么，真的都系于此。

turns.en: And clearly the other thing to watch is those November 3rd midterms. And more importantly, a lot of the geopolitical developments that might happen prior to them.
turns.zh: 而显然另一件要关注的事情是 11 月 3 日的中期选举。更重要的是，在中期选举之前可能发生的许多地缘政治进展。

turns.en: Will the administration be able to sort out some sort of a short-term peace deal with Iran? Will they be able to work out a deal with Canada?
turns.zh: 政府能否与伊朗达成某种短期和平协议？他们能否与加拿大达成协议？

turns.en: A lot of different things are in play and the midterms become an inflection point for this. And so the week leading into this midterms is gonna be pretty interesting to watch.
turns.zh: 有很多不同的事情在进行中，而中期选举成为这一切的拐点。所以进入中期选举的这一周将会相当有意思。

turns.en: All right, Patrick, let's turn to this week's positioning pulse. What stands out the most in this week's Scott Report? Well, Michelle, we definitely have to talk about corn because the USDA corn production forecast was raised to 234 million bushels.
turns.zh: 好的，Patrick，让我们转向本周的仓位脉搏（Positioning Pulse）。本周的 Scott Report 中最突出的是什么？——嗯，Michelle，我们绝对得谈谈玉米，因为 USDA 的玉米产量预测被上调到了 2.34 亿蒲式耳。

turns.en: It's a higher yield, less support of the bullish scarcity story. This is happening after just a few weeks ago. We saw some of the highest positioning scores for large speculators in terms of being bullishly positioned on corn.
turns.zh: 这是更高的单产，对多头所依赖的稀缺性叙事构成了更少的支撑。而这一切发生在几周之前我们才看到大型投机者在玉米上的多头仓位分数达到最高水平之一之后。

turns.en: So we saw roughly 166,000 net contracts sold over the last two weeks, both long liquidation and fresh shorting. So we are clearly seeing traders being shaken out of this trade.
turns.zh: 所以我们在过去两周里看到大约 16.6 万手净合约被卖出，既有多头平仓，也有新的做空。所以我们清楚地看到交易者被从这个交易中震出来了。

turns.en: It's very evident the way that the price is dropping. This went from a very bullish environment for these ag stories to now aggressively being washed out.
turns.zh: 从价格下跌的方式来看，这一点非常明显。这些农产品故事从一个非常看涨的环境，变成了现在被激进地清洗出去。

turns.en: This is certainly one that continue to watch in the weeks to come. Well, that's where we're gonna wrap up this week's trading desk. I'm Patrick Suresna.
turns.zh: 这肯定是未来几周需要继续关注的一个。好了，本周的交易台（Trading Desk）就到这里。我是 Patrick Ceresna。
